translation_notes: 2026-08-28 (revision after the interpolated-datatype fix): the gap this example documented is CLOSED. `f"{v}"^^{dt}` now transpiles to Literal(f"{v}", datatype=dtype(dt)), so the 14 runtime-datatype Literals whose VALUE IS ALREADY A str are now written in notation: string / integer / float / double / decimal / time / date / datetime / curie / uri / the three branches of map_uri_or_curie / _map_default_range_special_case. With the URIRef already in notation that is 15 of the 18 term constructors. Classification raised not-expressible -> awkward; driver re-run, RDFEVAL-VERDICT equivalent (module-state, demo_graph)

2026-08-28: str-valued is the load-bearing condition, and it holds here -- the base IfAbsentProcessor._map_to_default_value (corpus, packages/linkml/src/linkml/generators/common/ifabsent_processor.py:89-145) regex-matches ifabsent_default_value, so every default_value / hour / year reaching these methods is a str. For a str, `f"{v}"` is v itself and Literal(v, datatype=dt) already takes the lexical path, so the two terms are identical -- verified term-by-term with .n3() over all 19 demo values

2026-08-28: the two boolean branches deliberately STAY Python. Literal(True, datatype=xsd:boolean) has lexical form "true" whereas f"{True}" is "True". Measured: today they still compare equal, because rdflib's boolean lexical parser lowercases and NORMALIZE_LITERALS then rewrites "True" back to "true" -- but that equality is an artefact of rdflib's normalisation, not of the notation: with rdflib.NORMALIZE_LITERALS = False (a supported global) the rewrite yields "True"^^xsd:boolean against the original's "true"^^xsd:boolean, i.e. a different term. The str-valued branches above are immune to that switch. Rewriting a Python VALUE as a lexical form is the trap the interpolated-datatype form does not remove
2026-08-28: Literal(permissible_value_name) (map_enum_default_value) also stays Python -- a bare literal from a runtime value has no out-of-island form; that gap is untouched

2026-08-28: what the notation buys here is honestly small. `f"{default_value}"^^{ShaclDataType.STRING.uri_ref}` is no shorter and no clearer than `Literal(default_value, datatype=ShaclDataType.STRING.uri_ref)`; the module is a term factory that never asserts a triple, so there is no g{} island to amortise the notation. Hence awkward rather than directly-expressible: expressible, but the notation is at best a wash on this code shape
--- notes from the first review wave (kept for the record; the first one is superseded by the 2026-08-28 revision above) ---

17 of the 18 term constructors are Literal(value, datatype=ShaclDataType.X.uri_ref): the datatype is a RUNTIME lookup through linkml's ShaclDataType enum, and ldpy has no interpolated-datatype form -- verified: f"{x}"^^xsd:time transpiles, but f"{x}"^^{dt} is rejected with "type de donnee attendu apres '^^'". This is the concrete language gap this example documents

expressing them would mean inlining the enum (f"{year}-{month}-{day}"^^xsd:date and so on), which is rejected as unfaithful: ShaclDataType is a shared domain abstraction and the inlining would erase the STRING / CURIE / NCNAME / JSON_POINTER / JSON_PATH / SPARQL_PATH distinctions, all six of which resolve to xsd:string
Literal(permissible_value_name) with no datatype also stays Python: bare {expr} coercion only exists inside g{} islands

the single op the notation does reach: URIRef(self.schema_view.expand_curie(default_value)) -> f<{self.schema_view.expand_curie(default_value)}> (exact, since no @base is in scope); `from rdflib import Literal, URIRef` loses URIRef. Arguably no clearer than the original -- same observation as the pyRdfa _URI example
no g{} island anywhere: the module is a term factory, it never asserts a triple

context shim: linkml is not installed; context.py holds ShaclDataType verbatim, a trimmed IfAbsentProcessor base (the class constants + constructor the region reaches), model stand-ins for the annotation-only names, and a DemoSchemaView. Import lines only, identical on both sides

demo harness added identically to both representations: it calls all 19 literal-producing paths (including both special-case branches of map_uri_or_curie/map_curie/map_uri) into a module-level demo_graph, and prints the tuple-returning and NotImplementedError paths so stdout is compared too
